newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica suit joined by 60 local govts - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica suit joined by 60 local govts - lawyer.

text.p: More than 60 local governments in California have joined San Francisco in suing BankAmerica Corp for allegedly mismanaging municipal bond funds, a lead attorney in the case said on Wednesday.
San Francisco Deputy City Attorney Matt Davis said a complete list of plaintiffs would be compiled in the coming days. "We're at more than 60 (plaintiffs)," he said.

San Francisco and California's attorney general sued the BankAmerica unit Bank of America in May, alleging that the nation's third largest bank overcharged issuers, failed to return unclaimed funds from bond trust accounts, and improperly invested funds from some of the accounts.
Bank of America maintains that the investments it made were appropriate, and that it has fully returned unclaimed funds from the bond accounts.
The San Francisco suit has been joined by the counties of Alameda, Contra Costa, El Dorado, Marin, Nevada, Riverside, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Sonoma, Solano and Tulare.

The suit has also been joined by the cities of Belmont, Burbank, Emeryville, Fairfield, Folsom, Foster City, Gilroy, Glendale, Industry, Inglewood, Menlo Park, Pasadena, Pleasanton, Richmond, San Carlos, San Rafael, Santa Rosa, San Bernardino, Vallejo and Ventura.
Many other municipalities, local water districts and redevelopment agencies have joined the case.

The San Francisco and state lawsuits were based on a so-called "whistle-blower" complaint filed under seal in April 1995 by Patrick Stull, a former vice president for corporate trust at Bank of America.
